titulo_es: Inversion after negative adverbials (Never have I…, Not only…)
descripcion_es: Subject-auxiliary inversion after negative or restrictive expressions: Never have I…, Not only…, Hardly… when, Little did they know.
resumen: When a sentence begins with a negative or restrictive adverbial (never, rarely, not only, hardly, only then…), the auxiliary goes before the subject, as in a question. It is an emphatic, formal device, very useful in presentations and written texts.

explicacion.texto: The structure is: negative adverbial + auxiliary + subject + main verb. If the normal sentence has no auxiliary (present or past simple), add do/does/did, just as in questions: I rarely see him → Rarely do I see him.

filas: Never / Never before
Never have I seen such a crowd.
I have never seen such a crowd.
Rarely / Seldom
Seldom does she complain.
She seldom complains.
Not only… but (also)
Not only did he lie, but he also blamed me.
He not only lied but also blamed me.
Hardly / Scarcely… when
Hardly had we sat down when the phone rang.
We had hardly sat down when the phone rang.
No sooner… than
No sooner had she left than it started to rain.
She had no sooner left than it started to rain.
Little
Little did they know what awaited them.
They had no idea what awaited them.
Under no circumstances / On no account
Under no circumstances should you open this door.
You should not open this door under any circumstances.
Only then / Only when / Only after
Only when I got home did I realise.
I only realised when I got home.
Not until
Not until the next day did we hear the news.
We didn't hear the news until the next day.

items: With Hardly, Scarcely and No sooner, the past perfect is usually used in the first part; Hardly and Scarcely go with when (or before) and No sooner goes with than.
With Only when, Only after and Not until, the inversion happens in the MAIN clause, not in the subordinate clause: Only when he apologised did she forgive him.
With Not only, the second part (but also) has normal word order.
With the verb be, no auxiliary is needed: Never was he so happy.

explicacion.texto: If the adverbial is not at the beginning, there is no inversion: I have never seen it. There is no inversion either if only modifies the subject: Only Tom knew the answer (not “Only did Tom know”).

ejemplos.frase: Never before had the city witnessed such a protest.
ejemplos.traduccion: Nunca antes había presenciado la ciudad una protesta así.

ejemplos.frase: Not only is the plan expensive, but it is also unrealistic.
ejemplos.traduccion: El plan no solo es caro, sino que además es poco realista.

ejemplos.frase: Hardly had the concert begun when the lights went out.
ejemplos.traduccion: Apenas había empezado el concierto cuando se apagaron las luces.

ejemplos.frase: Little did I suspect that she was my cousin.
ejemplos.traduccion: Poco podía sospechar yo que era mi prima.

ejemplos.frase: On no account must the patient be left alone.
ejemplos.traduccion: Bajo ningún concepto se debe dejar solo al paciente.

ejemplos.frase: Only after the vote did the minister admit the error.
ejemplos.traduccion: Solo después de la votación admitió el ministro el error.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Never I have seen such a mess.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Never have I seen such a mess.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In Spanish it is enough to put “nunca” first; in English you must invert the auxiliary and the subject.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Rarely she goes out at night.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Rarely does she go out at night.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In the present and past simple you must add do/does/did, and the verb goes back to the base form.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Only when he arrived we started.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Only when he arrived did we start.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The inversion goes in the main clause, not in the clause after only when.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: No sooner had we arrived when it began to snow.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: No sooner had we arrived than it began to snow.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: No sooner goes with than; hardly and scarcely, with when.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: negative adverbial + auxiliary + subject + main verb. The clue is Never at the beginning of the sentence. The auxiliary have moves in front of I and the participle seen stays after it: Never have I seen. In Spanish it is enough to put “nunca” first, which is why the typical mistake is to keep I have.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After never at the beginning, the auxiliary goes before the subject.
ejercicios.traduccion: Nunca había visto una puesta de sol tan bonita.

por_opcion.I have seen: Incorrect: with never at the beginning you must invert; this is the typical mistake mentioned in the card.
por_opcion.have I seen: Correct: auxiliary before the subject after initial never.
por_opcion.I saw: Incorrect: the inversion is missing; with the past simple you would need did (Never did I see…).
por_opcion.seen I have: Incorrect: the participle does not go first; the order is auxiliary + subject + participle.

glosario.definicion_l: of a declining industry or technology · providing for termination

ejercicios.frase: No sooner had he sat down ___ the doorbell rang.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card that no sooner goes with than, while hardly and scarcely go with when. The clue is No sooner at the beginning, already with the inversion had he sat down. The word that introduces the second action is than, because no sooner is originally a comparative (“no earlier… than”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: No sooner is used with than.
ejercicios.traduccion: Nada más sentarse, sonó el timbre.

por_opcion.when: Incorrect: when goes with hardly and scarcely, not with no sooner (a typical mistake mentioned in the card).
por_opcion.than: Correct: no sooner… than is the fixed combination.
por_opcion.that: Incorrect: that does not form this correlation.
por_opcion.then: Incorrect: then is confused with than because they look alike, but it does not form the structure.

glosario.definicion_l: a push button at an outer door that gives a ringing or buzzing signal when pushed

ejercicios.frase: Only when the results came out ___ how serious the problem was.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: with only when the inversion happens in the main clause, not in the clause after only when. The clue is that Only when the results came out is already a complete clause without inversion; the main clause comes after it. As it is in the past simple, did is added and the verb goes back to the base form: did we realise.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With only when, the inversion happens in the main clause and did is added.
ejercicios.traduccion: Solo cuando salieron los resultados nos dimos cuenta de lo grave que era el problema.

por_opcion.we realised: Incorrect: the inversion in the main clause is missing (a typical mistake mentioned in the card).
por_opcion.did we realise: Correct: inversion with did in the main clause.
por_opcion.we did realise: Incorrect: did is there, but it is not inverted with the subject; the auxiliary must go first.
por_opcion.realised we: Incorrect: in this inversion, it is not the lexical verb that goes first, but an auxiliary (did).

ejercicios.frase: Seldom ___ my grandmother watch television; she prefers the radio.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: if the sentence has no auxiliary (present or past simple), add do, does or did. The clue is Seldom at the beginning, the subject my grandmother (third person singular) and the verb watch in the base form after it. That is why the auxiliary is does, which carries the present and third-person marking.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Present simple with a third-person subject: use does and the verb in the base form.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi abuela rara vez ve la televisión; prefiere la radio.

errores_previstos.respuesta: do
errores_previstos.explicacion: With a third-person singular subject the auxiliary is does.

errores_previstos.respuesta: did
errores_previstos.explicacion: The sentence is in the present (prefers); did would be past.

errores_previstos.respuesta: is
errores_previstos.explicacion: Be cannot be the auxiliary for watch in the present simple; you need does.

ejercicios.frase: Little ___ they know that the house had been sold.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: little with a negative meaning at the beginning requires inversion. The clue is Little at the start, the subject they, the verb know in the base form and the past perfect had been sold, which places the sentence in the past. As the verb is in the past simple, the auxiliary is did: Little did they know.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Little with a negative meaning in the past simple requires did before the subject.
ejercicios.traduccion: Poco sabían ellos que la casa había sido vendida.

errores_previstos.respuesta: do
errores_previstos.explicacion: The story is in the past (had been sold); you need did.

errores_previstos.respuesta: had
errores_previstos.explicacion: Had would need a participle (known); with know in the base form, the auxiliary is did.

errores_previstos.respuesta: knew
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb know is already in the sentence; the gap is for the auxiliary did.

ejercicios.frase: Scarcely had the train left the station ___ it broke down.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: hardly and scarcely go with when, while no sooner goes with than. The clue is Scarcely at the beginning, with the inversion had the train left. When is accepted, and so is before, which expresses the same idea of immediacy. What is not accepted is than, which is reserved for no sooner.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Scarcely… when (or before) expresses that something happened immediately afterwards.
ejercicios.traduccion: Apenas había salido el tren de la estación cuando se averió.

errores_previstos.respuesta: than
errores_previstos.explicacion: Than goes with no sooner; with scarcely, use when (or before).

errores_previstos.respuesta: that
errores_previstos.explicacion: That does not form this time correlation.

errores_previstos.respuesta: then
errores_previstos.explicacion: Then does not introduce the second action in this structure.

glosario.definicion_l: only a very short time before · almost not

ejercicios.frase: Under no circumstances ___ visitors feed the animals.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: after under no circumstances comes an auxiliary, usually a modal, before the subject. The clue is the negative expression at the beginning and the verb feed in the base form. Should, must, may and can are accepted, because they are all modals that express prohibition or obligation in this context; should and must are the most common in notices.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After under no circumstances, a modal goes before the subject.
ejercicios.traduccion: Bajo ninguna circunstancia deben los visitantes dar de comer a los animales.

errores_previstos.respuesta: are
errores_previstos.explicacion: Be cannot be followed by feed in the base form; after the negative adverbial you need a modal such as should or must.

errores_previstos.respuesta: visitors
errores_previstos.explicacion: The subject is already after the gap; the inverted auxiliary is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: musn't
errores_previstos.explicacion: Besides being misspelt (mustn't), it doubles the negation, because under no circumstances is already negative.

ejercicios.frase: I have never been so embarrassed.
respuestas: Never have I been so embarrassed.
Never before have I been so embarrassed.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: never goes first and the auxiliary have is inverted with the subject. The clue is the original sentence I have never been, which already has an auxiliary (have). Starting with Never, you get Never have I been so embarrassed. Never before have I been, which adds emphasis, is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Never goes first and the auxiliary have is inverted with the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Never I have been so embarrassed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It puts never first but does not invert; this is the typical mistake mentioned in the card.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Never have I never been so embarrassed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It repeats never; the negation is already at the beginning.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Never did I have been so embarrassed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The sentence already has an auxiliary (have); do not add did.

glosario.definicion_l: cause to be embarrassed; cause to feel self-conscious · hinder or prevent the progress or accomplishment of

ejercicios.frase: We rarely eat out during the week.
respuestas: Rarely do we eat out during the week.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: in the present simple, add do before the subject. The clue is the original sentence We rarely eat, with no auxiliary, and the instruction to start with Rarely. With we the auxiliary is do and the verb stays in the base form: Rarely do we eat out.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In the present simple, add do before the subject.
ejercicios.traduccion: Rara vez comemos fuera entre semana.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Rarely we eat out during the week.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It puts rarely first but does not invert; this is the typical mistake mentioned in the card.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Rarely eat we out during the week.
errores_previstos.explicacion: In modern English the lexical verb is not inverted; do is added.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Rarely does we eat out during the week.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With we the auxiliary is do, not does.

glosario.significado: comer fuera, comer en un restaurante

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence starting with “Not until”.
ejercicios.frase: She didn't call me until midnight.
respuestas: Not until midnight did she call me.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: with not until the complement goes first and the main clause is inverted with did. The clue is the original sentence She didn't call me until midnight and the instruction to start with Not until. The negation moves to not until midnight, so didn't disappears and you get did she call, an inverted affirmative.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Not until + complement goes first and the main clause is inverted with did.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Not until midnight she called me.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The inversion in the main clause is missing: did she call.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Not until midnight didn't she call me.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It doubles the negation; not until is already negative, so use did.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Not until midnight did she called me.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After did the verb is in the base form: call.

ejercicios.frase: Not only she speaks French, but she also speaks Russian.
respuestas: Not only does she speak French, but she also speaks Russian.
Not only does she speak French, but she speaks Russian too.
Not only does she speak French but she also speaks Russian.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: after not only at the beginning there is inversion, and in the present simple does is added. The clue is Not only she speaks, with no auxiliary and no inversion. The first part becomes Not only does she speak French, with the verb in the base form; the second part, with but also, keeps normal word order. Variants with also or too, and with or without a comma, are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The first part, after not only, needs does + subject + base verb.
ejercicios.traduccion: No solo habla francés, sino que también habla ruso.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Not only she speaks French, but she also speaks Russian.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: after initial not only you need does + subject + base verb.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Not only does she speaks French, but she also speaks Russian.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After does the verb is in the base form: speak.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Not only does she speak French, but also does she speak Russian.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The inversion only affects the not only part; after but also, normal word order is used.

ejercicios.frase: Hardly we had finished dinner when the guests arrived.
respuestas: Hardly had we finished dinner when the guests arrived.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: after hardly at the beginning, the auxiliary had goes before the subject, and hardly goes with when. The clue is Hardly at the start and the past perfect we had finished. Had is inverted with we: Hardly had we finished dinner when the guests arrived.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After hardly at the beginning, the auxiliary had goes before the subject.
ejercicios.traduccion: Apenas habíamos terminado de cenar cuando llegaron los invitados.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Hardly we had finished dinner when the guests arrived.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: after initial hardly you must invert had and the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Hardly had we finished dinner than the guests arrived.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The inversion is right, but it changes when to than; hardly goes with when.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Hardly did we finish dinner when the guests arrived.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The sentence already has an auxiliary (had); it is not replaced by did.

respuestas: On no account must you tell him
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: on no account + modal + subject + verb. The clue is the expression On no account (Spanish “bajo ningún concepto”), which is a negative adverbial and requires inversion. The modal must moves in front of you and the verb tell stays after it: On no account must you tell him.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: On no account + modal + subject + verb.

errores_previstos.respuesta: On no account you must tell him
errores_previstos.explicacion: It puts the negative expression first but does not invert the modal and the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: On account no must you tell him
errores_previstos.explicacion: It breaks up the fixed expression on no account.

respuestas: Never had she felt so alone
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: never + had + subject + participle. The clue is Never together with the past perfect had felt. The auxiliary had moves in front of she and the participle felt stays after it: Never had she felt so alone.
ejercicios.traduccion: Nunca se había sentido tan sola.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Never she had felt so alone
errores_previstos.explicacion: It puts never first but does not invert; it is a literal copy of Spanish word order.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Never had felt she so alone
errores_previstos.explicacion: Only the auxiliary is inverted; the participle goes after the subject.

descripcion_larga_es: When a sentence begins with a negative or restrictive adverbial (never, rarely, not only, hardly, only then, under no circumstances…), English places the auxiliary before the subject, as in a question. It is an emphatic, formal device that is highly valued in presentations and written texts. It is difficult for Spanish speakers because in Spanish it is enough to put “nunca” first without changing anything else.

contexto.que_es: It is the inversion of auxiliary and subject that happens when a negative or restrictive adverbial goes at the beginning of the sentence. The structure is adverbial + auxiliary + subject + main verb; if the normal sentence has no auxiliary (present or past simple), do, does or did is added and the verb goes back to the base form.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is one of the most recognisable features of educated, emphatic English, and it appears frequently in speeches, opinion articles, reports and advanced-level exams. Used well, it gives force to an argument (Not only… but also…); used badly (Never I have seen…), it gives away a literal translation from Spanish. Some fixed combinations (no sooner… than, hardly… when) are often tested.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is used in a formal register or for emphasis, especially at the beginning of a paragraph or an argument. The signals are never, rarely, seldom, little, hardly, scarcely, no sooner, not only, not until, only when and expressions such as under no circumstances or on no account. Spanish speakers tend to put the adverb first without inverting, or to invert in the wrong clause after only when and not until.
